workload patterns can be used to predict workload and that this prediction can be used to configure cloud services.

1) the proposed approach can predict the workload of cloud services with an accuracy that is comparable to the state of the art; 2) the workload patterns are useful to improve the efficiency of the prediction process; 3) the workload patterns can be used to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the configuration process.
we propose a prediction-based auto-scaling technique that combines a novel pattern-matching approach with a traditional prediction solution to meet the requirements for accuracy and efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to predict workload patterns for quality-driven dynamic cloud service configuration and auto-scaling.
the development of an accurate and efficient workload prediction technique for the dynamic cloud service configuration and auto-scaling problem.

a novel solution that combines the advantages of a collaborative filtering approach with the benefits of a rulebased approach to provide a scalable, accurate, and efficient prediction of workload and service performance for dynamic cloud service configuration and auto-scaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is an accurate and efficient prediction-based technique for quality-driven dynamic cloud service configuration and auto-scaling.
the proposed approach can be used to improve the performance of a dynamic cloud service configuration and auto-scaling solution.
the workload patterns approach is a promising technique to support the dynamic configuration and auto-scaling of cloud services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
workload patterns can be used to predict the workload of a cloud service and can be used to configure and scale cloud infrastructure.
workload patterns provide an accurate and fast prediction of future workload and are a good starting point for the initial configuration of cloud service performance management.
we have proposed a new approach to workload pattern matching that is more accurate and efficient than previous techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of pattern matching and traditional collaborative filtering can be used to predict future workloads and thus improve dynamic cloud service configurations.
the combination of pattern matching and collaborative filtering is an efficient and accurate solution to the problem of workload prediction.

a pattern-matching approach to workload prediction is more accurate than traditional approaches, and that the combination of the pattern matching with the traditional approaches is more efficient than either approach in isolation.
